Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+4b,$ find $\lambda .$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+4b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $4b.$ So, we first draw the vector $4b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931259/assets/d8fdfb800bd9bbb179d51115b86823d99029732fee9810281b9c587a32376993.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $4b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=4|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-4a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =4b-4a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+4b=-4a+4b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-4
$$
